rationale: No race telemetry is available for this iteration. Iteration 0's draft was lost to an output-length cutoff, so there is no measured evidence yet and this is a first-principles baseline. Geometry: five line sensors at x = -0.02, -0.01, 0, 0.01, 0.02 m cover about 0.8 tape widths, placed 0.05 m ahead of the axle so they read the line before the wheels reach it. Sensor size 0.012 m covers the 25 mm tape without over-smearing bends. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m give moderate turn authority; body 0.12 x 0.18 m and mass 0.8 kg keep yaw inertia modest and well inside the off-track limit. Controller: sensor weights (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2) follow the sensor's lateral offset, so a line on the left gives a positive signal and steers left, as the contract requires. kp = 3 gives about 1050 PWM per unit signal, firm but not saturating. ki = 0.1 is kept small to avoid integral wind-up on bends. kd = 0.3 damps sensor-driven oscillation. base_speed = 1.5 targets the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish within 3 s while leaving margin for cornering. line_loss = last_direction so the robot keeps turning the way it was going when the line is lost at the edge of a bend. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend with modest error; the slalom and unseen tracks may show oscillation or line loss, which the next telemetry should expose. All measurements are requested so the next iteration can tune kp, kd and base_speed against measured rms_error, steering_oscillation and line_loss_events.
